messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran the midnight GPU sweep and saw a cluster-wide spike in DCGM ECC/Xid alerts between 00:12-00:18 UTC. Lots of single-sample blips, but ~12 cards crossed the alert threshold and triggered drains.

dan: saw the alert floods in grafana too. are these correlated to the kernel patch rolled last week? or is it thermal/noise?

maria: good question. I pulled the sweep logs and correlated node:ssd, driver versions, and card age. 10/12 have driver 525.x, but two are 470.x legacy nodes in eu-west1. timestamps line up with our nightly batch eviction window.

kevin: can you paste the raw probe output for one example?

maria: sure — example line from the sweep probe:```
2026-03-18T00:14:08Z node=gpu-eu-12 card=3 dcgm_ecc_count=1 dcgm_xid=0 temp=68C power=180W
2026-03-18T00:14:12Z node=gpu-eu-12 card=3 dcgm_ecc_count=0 dcgm_xid=0 temp=69C
```

maria: these were single-sample increments; exporter's scrape interval caught them but prom rule fired on 1m rate.

dan: sounds like false positives from sampling granularity. our current prom rule is `dcgm_ecc_count > 0` with `for: 1m`. maybe too sensitive.

kevin: agree. proposal: change to a streak-based suppression: require >=2 consecutive 1m samples OR aggregate over 3m with rate > 0. Thresholds: `for: 3m` + `increase severity only if node.card.flake_count > 3 in 24h`.

maria: also noticed region skew — us-west nodes had almost none, eu-west and ap-south heavier. could be different batch timing or thermal profile in eu racks. if we relax rules we must not miss true failures.

ops-qa: +1 on streak heuristic. We should also add a short-lived annotation on alerts with `sample_count` and `last_seen_delta` so oncall can triage quickly. Something like: `annotations: { sample_count: '{{ $value | sample_count }}', last_seen: '{{ humanizeDuration ... }}' }`.

kevin: drafted a PromQL snippet to propose:```promql
sum_over_time(dcgm_ecc_count[3m]) by (node, card) >= 2
```
This coalesces transients and only triggers on repeated events.

maria: ran the snippet against last 30d — reduces alert volume by ~72% while keeping known true positives. I can drop the query into a test rule in staging.

dan: important to quantify cost impact: every unnecessary drain costs us capacity and provisioning churn. quick calc: 12 drains x avg 3h churn = 36 GPU-hours lost overnight. at $1.8/GPU-hour that's ~$65 hit just last night, plus disruption to queues.

kevin: thanks for the calc. if we reduce false drains by 70% we save ~25 GPU-hours/night on similar events. worth it.

maria: next actions: 1) push test prom rule to staging with `sum_over_time` 3m; 2) add alert annotation fields and a severity ramp (page only if sustained 30m or >5 events/hr); 3) run targeted re-sweep for the 12 cards and collect kernel/firmware/drain history; 4) file follow-up to investigate eu rack cooling logs.

ops-qa: can we also add a one-off temporary suppression during nightly eviction window? i.e., mute low-severity ECC alerts between 00:10-00:20 unless they exceed the sustained threshold.

maria: yes — I'll add a silence rule that auto-expires after 30m and only applies to severity=low AND nodes in `eviction-window`. We'll keep a conservative fallback so we don't ignore real hardware failures.

sre-bot: Automated sweep summary uploaded: https://redwood-internal/sweeps/2026-03-18/3298765432 — includes per-card spike histograms and CSV export.

dan: please post the staging rule PR and the sweep CSV. I'll review and we can roll to prod tomorrow if staging looks good.

maria: PR created: https://git.redwood/internal/infra/alerting/pulls/432 — contains prom rule + annotations + silence schedule. tagging @kevin for review.

kevin: reviewing now. if all green let's target a 10:00 UTC rollback window in case we need to revert.

maria: thanks team — will follow up with the eu rack cooling tickets and a short runbook update for oncall with the new heuristics. :white_check_mark:
